parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment begins with "2) try to provide some intuition as to why this alternative architecture was interesting to consider beyond merely the empirical results." The "2)" is merely an item number within the review comment itself, not a reference to a specific section of the evaluated paper. The comment does not explicitly point to any section, table, figure, or unique part of the paper; the phrase "this alternative architecture" is a vague reference from which authors could only make an educated guess about which part is meant. However, the comment does clearly specify what needs to be addressed: providing intuition for the alternative architecture beyond empirical results, adding real-world evaluation instead of relying solely on 'simulated pixels', and discussing systems aspects such as training step, inference speed, and memory compared to other approaches. These are specific, actionable points. Thus, the comment specifies the issues well but lacks explicit grounding to a paper part, which corresponds to a mid-level rating on the rubric where authors cannot confidently determine which part is addressed despite the clear specification of what needs addressing.
